facts.fact: ITWeb says the Information Regulator oversees organisations' compliance with the Promotion of Access to Information Act (PAIA).
facts.system: Promotion of Access to Information Act

facts.fact: The Information Regulator, which oversees PAIA, introduced online reporting of PAIA complaints in January 2026, according to its CIO.
The regulator's CIO says Section 71 of the POPI Act, on decisions based solely on automated processing, is relevant as AI becomes more widely adopted.

ZAF.note: The regulator is only exploring AI applications; no tender, pilot or system in service stated.
The national AI policy is only said to be awaited; no drafting stated.
No locally built AI model, dataset or computing stated.

facts.fact: ITWeb, interviewing its CIO, describes the Information Regulator as the body overseeing compliance with POPIA and PAIA and at work.

ZAF.note: Fines mentioned are not tied to a named organisation; notifications received are not decisions settled.

facts.fact: The Information Regulator oversees compliance with the Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA) and has imposed administrative fines for POPIA violations, per its CIO.
The Information Regulator is at work overseeing POPIA, with a CIO speaking for it.

The regulator says it received 2,374 security compromise notifications in 2024/25, about 198 a month, and has about 200,000 information officer registrations; it says it has imposed administrative fines without naming any.
The Information Regulator launched an e-services platform in May 2024 and offers online registration, POPIA exemption applications, complaints and security compromise reporting, per its CIO.

ZAF.note: Single gateway and usage not stated for a national portal.

facts.fact: The Information Regulator introduced online reporting of POPIA complaints in October 2025 and PAIA complaints in January 2026, with no complaint counts given.

ZAF.note: ISO/IEC 42001 only being looked at by the regulator; no membership, adoption or rule stated.
